hyps.why: Raising an already large learning rate causes divergence, as in runs 7, 8 and 10 where all three datasets dropped.
Lowering an excessive learning rate restores stable training, as in runs 12 and 13 where all three datasets improved.
With a very small learning rate, 243 epochs undertrain the network, so a larger step helps, as in runs 1 and 2.
A very strong L2 penalty underfits, so weakening it helps a lot, as in runs 31 and 40.
Pushing an already strong L2 penalty higher increases underfitting, as in run 27.
Deeper networks are less stable at a high learning rate, as in run 65 where vehicle fell 38.8 points.
Shallower networks tolerate a high learning rate better, as in run 75 where segment and vehicle rose 24 and 36 points.
A larger batch means fewer update steps, which hurts when the learning rate is already tiny, as in run 50.
Very small batches give noisy gradients, so increasing the batch size tends to help, as in runs 42, 43 and 44.
Reducing an already large batch adds noise, as in runs 51, 52 and 60, and the benefit does not carry over from the low-batch case.
